sentences.text:
India Seeking To Issue A Writ Of Mandamus ... vs Unknown on
26 September, 2019
Author: G.Shyam Prasad

Bench: G.Shyam Prasad
 1
 Hon'Ble Sri Justice G.Shyam Prasad
 Writ Petition No. 13854 of 2019
Order:

This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India seeking to issue a writ of Mandamus directing the respondents to release the seized Mahindra Bolero bearing No. AP05 XH TR 6368 belongs to the petitioner.
2. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned Government Pleader for Home appearing for official respondents.
With the consent of both the counsel, the writ petition is being disposed of at the stage of admission.
3. The petitioner is the owner of the Mahindra Bolero bearing No.AP 05 XH TR 6368 used for transport of goods.
On 13.07.2019, the respondent police have seized the vehicle on the allegation of illegal transportation of Gutka and handed over to 2nd respondent.
A case in crime No.124 of 2019 was registered for the offences punishable under Sections 188, 270 and 273 IPC and Section 22 of COTPA, 54 r/w.59 of Food Safety and Standards Act.
5. It is the case of the petitioner that the said FIR against the petitioner has been quashed by order dated 23.09.2019 passed in Crl.P.no.52445 of 2019 by this Court.

The petitioner has not filed any proof of the proceedings of quash of FIR.
6.

Therefore, the petitioner may file the copy of the order dated 23.09.2019 passed in Crl.P.No.5244 of 2019, before the police concerned and on filing the copy of the order, the police shall release the vehicle by following due process of law.

In case if crime is not quashed, the police shall release the vehicle by following due process of law.
7.
Therefore, the petitioner is given liberty to prefer a representation to the police concerned for release of the vehicle.
8. With the above observations, the writ petition is disposed of.
No costs.
